expected_title: Probabilistic Methods for Nanosatellite Systems Engineering: A Lasercom Case Study
abstract: Applying current systems engineering methods to nanosatellites can result in overdesign- ing or mismanaging the typically higher risk tolerance of nanosatellite platforms. Emerg- ing systems engineering approaches (e.g. multidisciplinary optimization or Bayesian-based design) could address this gap. However, these approaches require use of integrated perfor- mance models. Integrated performance models with a validated set of input distributions and tools to use them do not yet exist for some complex systems such as laser communica- tions (lasercom) systems. In this paper, we present our work towards building a lasercom link analysis model with a validated set of input distributions, and apply it to several exam- ples to investigate whether the model enables improvements in systems engineering. The scope of this work is restricted to an initial subset of nanosatellite-based lasercom systems and related ground stations where we expect that the higher platform-speciﬁc variations such as unpredictable pointing error may make the approach especially useful. We build uncertainty-based lasercom performance models for the Nanosatellite Optical Downlink Experiment (NODE), a student project at MIT. We evaluate the utility of our new models for diﬀerent phases of systems engineering by prioritizing analysis and test activity through Sobol’ and gradient sensitivity analysis and Bayesian-based experiment design. While we focus on a nanosatellite lasercom example, the process for characterizing the input dis- tributions and modeling performance is generalizable to other lasercom systems or other multidisciplinary space systems.
